title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is extremely faint. It is a first draft of the list of equivalences written out cleanly on the next page (125), and only the skeleton can be read: items 1°–9° joined by ⇔ signs, with groups 𝒜^*(X)^? and 𝒜_*(X)^?, products X×Y, the case X=Y, and a map 𝒜_*(X)^? → A (an abelian variety). Reading it against p.125, the content is as follows.

Fix an equivalence relation τ on algebraic cycles, presumably adequate and lying between rational and algebraic equivalence. Let A^i(X)^a be the τ-classes of codimension-i cycles that are algebraically equivalent to zero. Grothendieck lists statements that he claims are equivalent:

1°) The intersection product A^i(X)^a × A^j(X)^a → A^{i+j}(X)^a is 'univ' (most plausibly: universally zero).
1° bis) The same for the exterior product into X×Y.
2°, 2° bis) The same for 0-cycles of degree 0: A_0(X)^a × A_0(Y)^a → A_0(X×Y)^a.
3°) Concretely: (x,y) − (x,b) − (a,y) + (a,b) ~_τ 0 for all points a, x of X and b, y of Y. This is the vanishing of exterior products of degree-0 zero-cycles.
3° bis) The same with X = Y, via the classes K^{ij}.
4°) On an abelian variety A: (x+y) − (x) − (y) + (0) ~_τ 0. Equivalently, x ↦ (x) − (0) is a homomorphism A → A_0(A)^τ, and it is surjective. Note that (x+y) − (x) − (y) + (0) is the Pontryagin product ([x]−[0]) * ([y]−[0]).
4° bis) The Albanese map A_0(A)^a → A is an isomorphism, with inverse the map of 4°.
5°) For every X, A_0(X)^a → Alb(X) is an isomorphism, possibly stated generically / after base extension.
6°) A_0(X×Y)^a → A_0(X)^a × A_0(Y)^a is bijective.

In modern terms, Grothendieck is characterising the adequate equivalence relations τ for which 0-cycles of degree 0 modulo τ are exactly the Albanese variety. The criterion is that τ kills products of algebraically trivial cycles, i.e. the second step F^2 of the (later) Bloch–Beilinson filtration. The key mechanism is that on an abelian variety the Albanese kernel is I*I, the square of the augmentation ideal under Pontryagin product. This page serves the cycle-theoretic programme of the dossier (standard conjectures, Hodge, Tate) by locating the 'Albanese' part of the Chow group.
errors: Taken with τ = rational equivalence over C, the equivalent statements are false. Mumford (1969) showed the Albanese kernel of a surface with p_g>0 is enormous, so (x+y)−(x)−(y)+(0) is not rationally trivial on an abelian surface in general. The page only makes sense as a set of equivalences for a hypothetical τ, or as a test of whether such an adequate τ can exist.

Some implications need care. 1° ⇒ 2° is marked only one-way on p.125. Passing from abelian varieties (4°) to arbitrary X (5°) requires the Albanese kernel of X to be generated by images of exterior or Pontryagin products, which is not immediate for arbitrary X. The text is too faint to see how Grothendieck intended to argue this.

ideas.what: On an abelian variety, the Albanese kernel of degree-0 zero-cycles is generated by (x+y)−(x)−(y)+(0), i.e. by Pontryagin products of two elements of the augmentation ideal
ideas.modern_name: Pontryagin filtration I^{*k} on CH_0 of abelian varieties; F^2 = Albanese kernel

ideas.what: Equivalence between vanishing modulo τ of exterior products of degree-0 zero-cycles, (x,y)−(x,b)−(a,y)+(a,b) ~ 0, and the Albanese map on A_0 modulo τ being an isomorphism for all varieties
ideas.modern_name: Characterisation of the second step F^2 of the Bloch–Beilinson filtration; Albanese kernel generated by exterior products

ideas.what: Searching for an adequate equivalence relation under which degree-0 zero-cycles become exactly the Albanese, and phrasing this as vanishing of intersection products of algebraically trivial cycles
ideas.modern_name: 'Albanese equivalence' / Samuel's question on adequate relations between rational and algebraic equivalence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Samuel (1958); later Jannsen's survey 'Equivalence relations on algebraic cycles' (2000)

missed.claim: Circa 1965–71 Grothendieck explicitly ties three things together: the vanishing of products of algebraically trivial cycles, the vanishing of exterior products of degree-0 zero-cycles, and Pontryagin squares on abelian varieties. He presents these as equivalent to the Albanese map being an isomorphism. This is essentially the F^2 / Albanese-kernel structure later made explicit by Bloch (1976) and the Bloch–Beilinson filtration, and it predates them.
missed.quote: 4°) Si A v.a. ... (x+y)−(x)−(y)+(0) ∼_τ 0 ... ⇔ 4° bis) A_0(A)^a → A est un isom.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it shows Grothendieck considering the Albanese kernel as generated by products before Mumford's 1969 counterexample and Bloch's work. It also frames 'does an adequate relation realising Alb exist?' as a question about products, a framing that is little discussed explicitly in the literature.

missed.claim: Items 5°–9° (general X, base change / 'générique', and the bijectivity of A_0(X×Y)^a → A_0(X)^a × A_0(Y)^a) are only sketched, and no proof of the full equivalence chain is written out.
missed.quote: 6°) Pr X, Y, l'hom A_0(X×Y)^a → A_0(X)^a × A_0(Y)^a (générique ...) est bijectif
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Giving a precise statement and proof of which adequate τ satisfies these conditions is a clean question that touches Jannsen's classification of adequate relations.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a nearly illegible draft. Its content, as clarified by the next page, is an early and explicit formulation of the Albanese kernel as the place where products of degree-0 cycles vanish, including the Pontryagin-square identity on abelian varieties. These ideas are now attributed to Bloch, Beauville and Bloch–Beilinson, so the page is interesting mainly historically and is not a hidden new theorem.
transcription_corrections: The superscript written 'ℚ' in the machine transcription is probably 'a' (algebraically trivial part) or 'τ', matching the clean version on p.125.
1°) should probably read A^i(X)^a × A^j(X)^a → A^{i+j}(X)^a, i.e. the intersection product, not a product written with 𝒜^*.
Items 3°/4° likely concern A_0, i.e. 0-cycles (written 𝒜_*), with X×Y and then X=Y, mirroring 2°/2° bis and 3° bis of p.125.
7°) '𝒜_*(X)^ℚ → A' is likely 'A_0(A)^a → A' (the Albanese map of an abelian variety, 4° bis on p.125).
